strategy.title: No plan reaches $90,000: the counted market tops out at $72,000
strategy.why: The only opening sells a $480 per-term attendance audit to accredited private English-language schools. The accreditation body lists 150 schools, each audits once per term, so even if every school bought inside the window the most it can bring is 150 x $480 = $72,000, below the $90,000 target. At the measured conversion (18 paid of 150 contacted) it brings about $8,640.

alternatives.title: Sell the audit to all 150 schools
alternatives.why: Caps at $72,000 gross even at 100% conversion; the measured 12% rate gives about $8,640.

steps.label: Ask the owner to lower the target to at most $72,000 (realistically about $8,640 at measured conversion), or find further independent openings to cover the remaining $18,000+

strategy.title: Sell the $480 student-visa attendance audit to accredited English-language schools
strategy.why: The objective is now $3,000 net after direct costs in 30 days with no up-front capital. reviews.reasons: Recomputed: buyerVolume (EVIDENCE) counts the whole market at 150 accredited schools, each auditing once per term, so at most one $480 sale per school inside 30 days: 150 x $480 = $72,000 gross (less $30 x 150 = $4,500 direct cost) < $90,000. 151+ deals would be needed (90,000/480 = 187.5, i.e. 188 deals), more than the counted population. This is a genuine constraint, not missing evidence: price, conversion (18/150 measured), fulfilment and settlement are all evidenced and the target still cannot be reached. At measured 12% conversion it brings about $8,640. No other opening is held. NO_PLAN with decisiveLinks [MARKET_VOLUME] and a TARGET constraint grounded in buyerVolume and price is correct; Brain's verdict (NOT_VIABLE, cap $72,000) agrees.
findings: The cap is if anything lower than $72,000: the 18 pilot schools that already paid $480 (pilot invoices 2026-11) have likely bought this term's audit, leaving about 132 schools, i.e. at most about $63,360 in the window.
Minor: the noPlan text says 151 deals are needed (echoing Brain's link basis); at $480 the target needs 188 deals. The conclusion is unchanged.

reviews.reasons: The stored contract is now $3,000 CONTRIBUTION (net after direct costs) in 30 days with $0 exposure, so the $90,000 NO_PLAN is correctly superseded. Recomputed: $480 - $30 = $450 net per audit; 7 x $450 = $3,150 is the minimum, 8 planned = $3,600 net ($3,840 collected - $240 cost). Price is buyers' own paid pilot invoices (EVIDENCE), a real purchase price. Volume: 150 counted schools, one audit each per term, against 8 needed; measured conversion 18/150 gives about 18 expected, more than double the need. Card payment at checkout, usable in 4 days (day 9), inside 30; $0 exposure and costs paid from receipts. Fulfilment is Brain-produced spreadsheet (PRODUCE_SPREADSHEET present), matching the card's delivery fact. Brain's links are all established from this offer's own record and I have no contradicting record. Brain's trace agrees (collected $3,840, net $3,600). EXECUTABLE is right.
findings: Possible double count: the 18 pilot buyers (invoices 2026-11) appear to come from the same 150-school directory and have likely already bought this term's audit, so the fresh pool is about 132, and if the 150 contacts behind the 12% were the whole directory, the remaining schools have already been approached once. Even so, 8 sales from ~132 needs only ~6% conversion; the plan should send to schools not in the pilot first and treat fewer than 8 paid by about day 20 as a stop signal.
SEND_A_MESSAGE and ISSUE_AN_INVOICE are NOT_CONNECTED and DISCOVER_LOCAL_BUSINESSES is UNREAD; outreach and card checkout must be connected before day 0/1.
Card humanHours 0.3 per sale (about 2.4 hours for 8) while members[].ownerHours is null; no hours ceiling applies.
